info.name: SPA Business API
info.description:
All 24 current /api/v1/business routes, including registration defined in customer.php. Grouped by workflow, with request payloads, saved success/error examples, role requirements, and implementation notes.

SETUP
1. Import this JSON into Postman.
2. Set base_url to your API root including /api/v1 (no trailing slash).
3. Set access_token from the existing Auth collection. Use an active business member token for management.
4. Send My businesses; select business_id. Fill other IDs from real list responses. IDs are ULIDs.
5. Open each request’s Documentation/description for comments; use the Examples dropdown to inspect saved responses without sending requests.

All response data is synthetic and based on controllers/resources, not live API execution. Dates are illustrative: update requested_date and offer dates before sending. Timezone offsets shown in responses are illustrative; persistence/serialization may normalize to UTC. Monetary amounts are integer minor units.

JSON does not support comments; explanatory comments live in descriptions and scripts so payloads stay valid JSON. GET/DELETE and no-input actions have no body. Requests inherit Bearer authentication. Successful create/propose scripts capture relevant IDs; no script sends follow-up requests.

Shared errors: 401 unauthenticated; 403 nonmember/insufficient role; 404 missing or mismatched resource; 422 input validation; 429 rate limit. Some controller abort(409/422) responses use Laravel’s default JSON error shape rather than the custom envelope. Relationship fields vary with what each endpoint loads.

Folders contain alternative state-changing actions, not a sequence for Collection Runner. Read descriptions before sending. Source: routes/api/business.php, routes/api/customer.php, business controllers, validators, resources, BookingService and AvailabilityService.

Media access: four business KYC uploads are separate from the four personal KYC uploads. Folder 07 contains related user profile/personal-document viewing requests. Public hero images use hero_image_url. Private document links require Bearer authentication.

item.name: 01 — Business profile & onboarding
item.description: Use an existing access_token from the Auth collection. Start with My businesses, then set business_id. Registration is optional and creates a new pending business; all four business KYC files are required. Do not run this folder as a single workflow.

request.description: Authenticated onboarding. Select a local PDF/JPG/JPEG/PNG for EACH of the four business KYC fields (max 5120 KB per file). Optional hero_image: JPG/JPEG/PNG/WebP, max 5120 KB. At least one locations[] entry is required. Submit locations[0][address], locations[0][city], locations[0][latitude], locations[0][longitude], and locations[0][service_availability] (home or on_site). Top-level address, city, latitude, and longitude are ignored. Optional category_ids[] must reference existing categories. Postman generates the multipart boundary: do not add Content-Type manually. Response KYC documents contain type/view_url pairs. The account receives the owner role. Saved responses are illustrative examples derived from the current backend, not captured live responses. Conditional relationship fields and timestamps can vary. Optional personal_kyc_document group: attach all four personal files using the bracketed form-data keys below. Each accepts PDF/JPG/JPEG/PNG up to 5120 KB. These paths are stored privately in the authenticated user’s kyc_document JSON column, separately from business KYC. Omit the group to preserve existing personal KYC; it is not included in the response. Optional dob (Text): YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 1995-04-15. When filled, updates the authenticated user’s date of birth in the registration transaction. Omitted, null, or blank preserves the existing DOB. ACCESSING UPLOADS: hero_image_url is public. data.kyc.documents[].view_url requires the business owner token. data.personal_kyc.documents[].view_url requires the uploading user’s token. Use GET with Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}} and Send, then open the response Preview tab for private files. A browser URL or tag alone does not attach your Bearer token; authenticated clients should fetch the file and use the returned bytes/blob. GET /users/me also returns personal_kyc links.

item.name: 05 — Booking requests & appointments
item.description:
Flow: customer requests a service/date → business lists pending requests → business proposes start times → customer confirms one time_id → awaiting_payment booking → payment confirms appointment → business progresses the booking.

Customer endpoints are outside this business collection: POST /bookings/requests with {"business_id":"…","service_id":"…","requested_date":"YYYY-MM-DD","people_count":1,"timezone":"Asia/Kathmandu"}; POST /bookings/requests/{booking_request}/confirm with {"time_id":"…"}, using the CUSTOMER token.

Set booking_request_id and requested_date from a real pending request. Propose and decline are alternative actions. Do not run the whole folder sequentially. Proposed slots do not reserve capacity; customer confirmation rechecks availability. The request expiry is not extended when times are proposed. All these business operations allow active members, including staff.

request.description:
Pending, unexpired requests only. starts_at is an array of datetime STRINGS, not an array of objects. End times come from current service duration. Set requested_date to the request date and slot_timezone_offset to the business timezone offset for that date. Use times inside business opening hours and outside closures.

Current limitations: proposing does not check date equality, duplicate slots, past start times, overlaps, end-before-closing, or slot-grid alignment. Confirmation generates availability for requested_date and matches HH:mm only. Choose matching dates and valid grid times yourself: service duration <=30 min → 15-min steps, <=60 → 30-min steps, otherwise 60-min steps, measured from opening. Availability currently blocks overlapping bookings across the entire business.

Captures the first returned time id as time_id for the customer confirmation request; a business token cannot confirm someone else’s request.

item.name: 07 — Personal KYC file access
item.description: Authenticated retrieval for personal documents uploaded during business registration. Public images use hero_image_url; personal/business KYC download URLs require Bearer authentication.

item.name: Get own profile and personal KYC links

request.description: Returns data.personal_kyc.documents with authenticated view URLs for the current user. Paths remain private. Uses the inherited Bearer token.

personal_document_type: pan, citizenship_front, citizenship_back, nid. Uses the current user’s Bearer token. GET a view_url returned by registration or GET users/me. Response is the actual PDF/image bytes; use Send, then open the response Preview tab. Returns 404 for unknown types, absent files, or a user without that document; 401 without authentication.
